subject: Concerto pilot packaging: staged-commit vs flex-hour topup
messages:
From: Alec Sullivan <alec.sullivan@concerto.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Concerto pilot: staged commit vs flex-hour topup?

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the cost breakdown you showed. We're coming up to the end of our 30-day pilot and have two internal paths under consideration. Before we lock anything in, can you share concrete pricing/packaging for both: 

- A staged-commit option (we commit to a short multi-month minimum in exchange for a discount and a capacity reservation).
- A flex-hour/top-up option (pay-as-you-go or small top-up buckets to extend the pilot).

Two constraints from my side: procurement wants lower upfront spend if possible, and engineering asked for a short SLA (99.x%) for the pilot window when we scale to >75 concurrent sessions.

Can you send a simple comparison (numbers + any minimums) and an updated SOW or quote we can circulate internally? Our procurement lead is procurement@concerto.ai and would like to be looped if we progress.

Best,
Alec
Alec Sullivan
Head of ML Platforms | Concerto AI

--
Note: we may need a 2-week extension on the pilot while procurement reviews — what's your typical runway for time-boxed evaluations?
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Sullivan <alec.sullivan@concerto.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concerto pilot: staged commit vs flex-hour topup?

Hi Alec — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary below and I attached a short offer doc with line-item pricing (Concerto_POC_Offer.pdf).

Option A — Staged Commit (recommended if you want predictable unit economics)
- Minimum: 3-month pilot extension (time-boxed)
- Committed spend: $45k/month (covers X GPU hours / Y token budget)
- Discount: 25% off pay-as-you-go rate for the committed term
- Capacity: reserved pool with priority routing during the pilot
- SLA: 99.9% availability for served requests above the 75-concurrency threshold (we can add a short SLA addendum in the SOW)

Option B — Flex Top-up (low upfront cost, higher marginal unit price)
- No minimum term: top-up buckets (25k token buckets or hourly pools)
- Rate: pay-as-you-go with 0% discount compared to commit pricing (higher per-token cost)
- Capacity: best-effort; we recommend burst reservations if you expect >75 concurrent sessions

Middle path — Staged-Minimum (we can special-case for pilots)
- 1-month deferred billing + 2-month commit (total 3 months), $38k/month effective (20% off)
- Lower upfront invoice in month 1 to help procurement sign-off

Next steps
- If procurement needs lower upfront spend, the Staged-Minimum is usually the fastest path.
- I'll loop Sales Ops to prepare an SOW and DocuSign envelope if you want to move forward.

Thoughts? Happy to hop on a 30-minute call today or tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Concerto_POC_Offer.pdf]
From: Alec Sullivan <alec.sullivan@concerto.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concerto pilot: staged-commit vs flex-hour topup?

Jonas — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups inline: 

> Option A — Staged Commit (recommended if you want predictable unit economics)

We like the price/commit math, but procurement will push back on the full $45k upfront for month one. Staged-Minimum looks promising. Two asks: 
1) Can you convert the committed spend to a token estimate (approx tokens/month) so our ML cost model can map it to expected inference volume?
2) Can the SLA language include a simple latency objective (p95 < 450ms for generated responses) while we're in the pilot? Engineering flagged that.

Procurement timeline: they want a signed SOW by Oct 8 to include in the Q4 budgeting wave. I'll loop in procurement@concerto.ai on the next response.

If you can prepare an SOW that shows: Staged-Minimum (2-month commit with month-1 deferred billing), token estimates, and an SLA bullet, we can circulate it to procurement and legal.

Alec

Hi Alec / procurement team — looping in Sales Ops to finalize an SOW and signature path. Per Jonas's Staged-Minimum approach we prepared an SOW that: 

- Implements a 2-month commit with month-1 deferred billing (invoice starts month 2).
- Shows estimated token usage: ~9M tokens/month (breakdown by model and expected avg prompt + gen lengths included in SOW).
- Adds SLA bullets: 99.9% availability and a p95 latency objective of <450ms for generated responses during pilot windows.

Attached: Redwood_Staged-Minimum_SOW.pdf (single-page summary). Once you confirm, we'll send the DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/ABC123456789

If procurement wants a lower-risk path we can also add a 30% holdback that releases on successful completion of the 2-month pilot (we've used that on other pilots). Let me know which of these three you prefer: 
- A) Staged-Minimum (deferred month-1 billing) — fastest
- B) Staged-Minimum + 30% holdback — procurement comfort
- C) Flex top-up (no commit) — slower to convert on price

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
